---
title: "Setup your machine for data science with R & Python"
subtitle: "A short guide to getting a fresh machine ready for the courses"
format: html
---

These guidelines are meant to be
followed during the live setup block at the start of the term, but also works
standalone if you come to class with an already-configured machine (skip ahead). 
We target **latest stable** versions of everything.

## 1. Install R

R is the language itself. Download the installer for your OS and follow the
instructions:

- macOS / Windows: <https://cran.r-project.org>
- Linux: use your package manager (`apt`, `dnf`…); see
  <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/linux/>

Check it works:

```r
R.version.string   # e.g. "R version 4.6.1"
```

## 2. Install Quarto

Quarto is our open-source scientific and technical publishing system. It turns
`.qmd` documents (and RevealJS slides!) into polished HTML, PDF, and more.

- Download: <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>

Check it works:

```bash
quarto --version   # e.g. 1.10.x
```

## 3. Install Positron (the IDE)

Positron is a next-generation data science IDE (a data-science-flavoured fork
of VS Code) that runs both R and Python.

- Download: <https://positron.posit.co/download.html>
- Choose the arm64 / x86_64 build that matches your machine.

Open Positron. On first launch it will offer to install the R extensions and
detect your R installation. Confirm both.

Positron will use this Quarto automatically for the Quarto preview/render.

## 4. Install R packages

Open the R console in Positron and run:

```r
install.packages("tidyverse")   # the core data-science collection
```

Verify with:

```r
library(tidyverse)
```

You should see the package startup message listing dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2,
readr, purrr, tibble, stringr, forcats.

By the time of the Reproducible Workflows course you will additionally want:

```r
install.packages(c("janitor", "naniar", "skimr", "renv", "knitr", "rmarkdown", "pins"))
```

(`renv` is used for dependency pinning; `pins` for data pinning; `janitor`/`naniar`/`skimr` feed the
data-cleaning and EDA labs.)

## 5. Some worthy Positron extensions (optional)

- **Air**: A Visual Studio Code extension for [Air](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/), an R formatter and language server, written in Rust.
- **Jarl**: A Visual Studio Code extension for [Jarl](https://jarl.etiennebacher.com), a fast R linter.
- **Posit Assistant**: An AI assistant for Positron. It uses functionality that is available only in Positron, so it will not work with other VS Code forks, like Cursor or Windsurf.
- **Pyrefly**: The Pyrefly extension uses Pyrefly to provide language server features for Python in VS Code. Please see <https://pyrefly.org> for more information.
- **Quarto**: A Visual Studio Code extension for the [Quarto](https://quarto.org) scientific and technical publishing system.
- **Quarto Wizard**: A Visual Studio Code extension that helps you manage your Quarto projects. It allows you to easily install Quarto extensions from the Quarto Extensions registry, GitHub repositories, URLs, or local paths.
- **Shiny**: This is an extension to help launch [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co) applications. Shiny is a package for Python and R that is designed to make it easy to build interactive web applications with the powerful data and scientific features of Python and R.

Some of them are pre-installed with Positron; other require opt-in installs via the *Extensions* panel.

## 6. Setup Python (optional)

In Positron:

- Open the palette with the keyboard shortcut `CMD + SHIFT + P`;
- Search for `Python: install Python via uv` and proceed.

More at <https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-07-08_positron-uv/>

## 7. Install Python packages (optional)

[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) is an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust.

You can easily install Python packages in dedicated virtual environments with `uv`. For example, to install the `pandas` and `numpy` packages, run in the Positron-integrated terminal:

```bash
uv init example
# Initialized project `example` at `/home/user/example`
uv add pandas numpy
```

More details can be found on the website.

## 8. Version checks, all together

For these courses, we will use R and Quarto.

Run in the R console:

```r
R.version.string
```

and in a terminal:

```bash
quarto --version
```

If both report a version, you are ready. Ask the instructor for help if any
step errors; resolve these at the start so the labs run smoothly.
